The kundi is a five-string plucked harp used by the Azande and related peoples of Central Africa, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs number 322.11. Its form belongs to the 'stopper-in-bottle' type of African bow harp: a wooden body has a spout-like opening at one end, the lower end of the neck is inserted into it to make a firm joint, and the base of the body is often wrapped in hide or carved as a human head. It is sounded by plucking, and traditionally it was played by young men and boys; the Nzakara also play a similar harp. The instrument is now in decline, and recordings of an elderly player were made in 1993.
孔迪豎琴音色溫潤而富有穿透力，具有明亮而不刺耳的特質。其音域寬廣，可涵蓋從低沉的: The kundi has a warm timbre that carries well, bright without being harsh. Its range is wide, from a deep fundamental to a clear high register, with a broad span of colour. Being a chordophone gives it an agile sound, and the resonance from the vibrating strings is deep and full. Against the Western classical harp the kundi has more of a folk character, warm and slightly desolate; against plucked instruments such as the pipa its sound is softer and more delicate, and the resonance lasts longer. It can carry a delicate lyrical melody and also build an ethereal, mysterious atmosphere, and it suits music of deep feeling and of meditation.
非洲弓形豎琴的早期形象見於尼羅河谷古埃及墓壁畫，最早可追溯至西元前3000年；西: Early images of African bow harps appear on ancient Egyptian tomb murals in the Nile valley, the earliest going back to 3000 BC; by 2500 BC the mature bow harp with a short shovel-shaped soundbox had appeared. New forms came after 1600 BC, and in the second half of the fifteenth century BC shoulder harps and angular harps appear; the angular harp later spread to West Africa and further south. According to Klaus Wachsmann's 1964 theory, the portable bow harp could have travelled down the Nile to East Africa and then branched into Central and West Africa, roughly within the equator, with Uganda at the centre. The kundi is the five-string bow harp of the Azande of Central Africa, traditionally played by young men and boys, and recordings of an elderly player were still being made in 1993.
